name: car_sedan
source: Geometry (wheelbase 2.70 m, track 1.56 m, wheel radius 0.317 m) matches data/models/car_sedan/car_sedan.rig.json. Mass (1500 kg curb weight) and a symmetric 50/50 front/rear static split are plausible round-number choices for a mid-size sedan (Genta, 'Motor Vehicle Dynamics', ch. 1 cites typical passenger-car curb weights of 1200-1700 kg and front/rear splits of roughly 50/50 to 60/40 - not a specific measured car). Suspension spring rates are chosen so the static-equilibrium compression sits at 1/3 of travel_max under this weight; damper rates target a ~0.35 damping ratio about that operating point (Milliken, 'Race Car Vehicle Dynamics', ch. 16). All 4 wheels reference data/tyres/passenger_car_225_45r17.json. Powertrain (PHYS-033 I3): data/engines/i4_2l_na.json -> dry clutch -> data/gearboxes/sedan_6mt.json -> open differential (final drive 4.06, a typical 2.0 L FWD value, range 3.9-4.4) -> FL/FR. This replaces the P3 placeholder's single final_drive_ratio = 10.0, which stood in for 1st gear x differential because there was no gearbox (vault PHYS-023); overall 1st is now 3.54 x 4.06 = 14.37. Clutch: kinetic capacity 300 N*m = 1.5 x engine peak torque (typical passenger-car reserve 1.3-1.8), static factor 1.15, progressive engagement vs pedal (diaphragm-spring-like). Aero: drag_area 0.68 m^2 = Cd 0.30 x A 2.27 m^2 (typical mid-size sedan). The manual_tcu driver aids (auto-clutch, auto-blip) default ON for gamepad play; see PHYS-033 I3 plan section 8. Auto-clutch post-shift close (owner test drive 2026-09-25, "a lot of wheel spin in 2nd"): sync_time_s 0.30 / max_sync_torque_nm 50 make the reclose torque-following (clutch capacity = engine torque + min(J_engine*|slip|/sync_time_s, 50 N*m), see AutoClutchDesc::sync_time_s) instead of a fixed-rate ramp to the full 300 N*m; max_sync_torque_nm 50 N*m (~25% of peak engine torque) caps what the synchronising term adds to the driven wheels on top of the engine's own torque; sync_time_s 0.30 is the time constant the engine speed converges on the input shaft with below that cap (tests/validation/test_powertrain_auto_clutch_shifts.cpp: 1->2 and 2->3 lock within 0.4-0.9 s). close_time_s 0.20 -> 0.10: the rate e_auto follows that target at, halved so the clutch picks the engine up right after dog-in instead of letting it flare further (WOT 2->3 probe: post-shift rpm peak 4926 -> 4578, max front kappa 0.085 -> 0.068).
